decisionSource: The two completed and integrated Iowa source-identity resolutions, read in full and verified by digest, against the four artifacts they stopped short of: the Iowa legal-design memo, the generated track-source relationships, the Master Library source-acquisition queue and the authoritative blocker ledger. No new legal research was performed and none was needed: both resolutions answered their questions from official primary authority and this record adjudicates what follows for six components.
whatThisDocumentIs: The component-remap decision that owns what two completed identity resolutions deliberately handed off. Both stopped at the same boundary — re-modelling a component rewrites the track-source relationships and the acquisition queue, which were forbidden paths for them — and each recorded its recommended corrections rather than applying them. This record decides those corrections, states the exact amendment each owning path must carry, and closes two acquisition keys without acquisition. It acquires nothing, materializes nothing, creates no receipt, edits no memo, regenerates no registry, implements no packet and asserts no counsel approval.

scopeOfThisJob.whyNothingElseIsWritten: The relationships, the packet-set manifests and the specifications are generated registries and are forbidden to a worker; the queue is generated by the Master Library reconciler and is never hand-maintained; the blocker ledger is a join over those; and the memo belongs to the Iowa legal-design owner. This job owns the decision and states each amendment precisely enough to be applied and checked, which is the only instrument available to it.
scopeOfThisJob.trackTouched: None. This record adjudicates six components across six tracks and writes only itself.

dependencies.whatItEstablished: That the document the repository calls 'Certification of Service by Mailing or Delivery' is not a document at all. It is a titled, boxed section on the last page of each of the five Rule 2.86 expungement applications. The Iowa Supreme Court characterises it in its own words as "the certificate of service section in the expungement applications (Rule 2.86—Forms 1–5)", and Iowa Ct. R. 16.316 — the rule that creates the obligation — expressly permits the certificate to be included on the last page of the document it accompanies and prescribes no form.
dependencies.whatItStoppedShortOf: Re-modelling the five components, retiring the identity, and closing the acquisition key. All three are decided here.

dependencies.whatItEstablished: That DCI-76 is page 1 of a single retained three-page Iowa Department of Public Safety packet whose remaining pages are DCI-77, measured at 1,076,864 bytes, sha256 321062c91b3d9e2c8f255d62d20186352a2b5884e0ccd4310a18a3a073d7f516, PDF 1.6, three unrotated 612 x 792 pages, an AcroForm with 45 terminal fields over 54 widget annotations, no XFA and no encryption. It also identified two self-contradictory fields on the queue row.
dependencies.whatItStoppedShortOf: Mapping the component to the packet page, pinning the digest on the relationship, closing the acquisition key and correcting the queue row. All four are decided here.

questionPresented.theQuestion: Six Iowa components point at documents that do not exist as such. What is each component's real target, and what exactly must change in the memo, the relationships, the queue and the ledger to say so?
questionPresented.whyItMattered: Both defects present as acquisition gaps and neither is one. Five components hold open an acquisition key for a form the Iowa Supreme Court has never prescribed, and a sixth holds one open for bytes the repository already retains and the adopted edition already records as acquired and adopted. Left alone they are permanent blockers that no download can ever clear, and they misdescribe what the participant is actually asked to do.
questionPresented.whyItWasOpen: Neither resolution could own the fix. Each named its recommended corrections and stopped at the relationship boundary, which is exactly right for a source-acquisition job and is why this job exists.

methodNote: No new retrieval. Both dependency records were read in full and pinned by digest, and every value carried forward here is quoted from one of them or read from a committed artifact in this repository. The chain from a memo field to a generated row was traced in the generator rather than assumed: sourceRelationships() in src/lib/rcap/legal-design/normalize.ts emits one row per official_pdf_fill component, carrying the component's officialFormId and officialSourceUrl and taking sha256 from the track's own officialSources entry whose url matches that component. That is why every amendment below is stated against the memo field that produces the row, not against the generated row itself.

determination.1_doTheSixComponentsShareOneDefect: They share a shape, not a cause. Both are an identity recorded at the wrong granularity: a part of a larger official artifact modelled as a standalone acquirable document. Iowa has now produced this pattern twice, which is consistent with a normalization pass that split multi-part official packets into per-section identities. The remedies differ because the artifacts differ — one part has no independent bytes and never will, the other has bytes that are already retained.
determination.2_certificationOfServiceTarget: Each of the five certificate_of_service components targets its own track's parent Rule 2.86 form, at a named page, as a section reference. The mapping is exactly one to one and no track shares a form with another: ia-901c2 to Form 1 page 3 of 3, ia-901c3 to Form 2 page 3 of 3, ia-12346 to Form 3 page 2 of 2, ia-12347 to Form 4 page 2 of 2, ia-7251 to Form 5 page 2 of 2.
determination.3_isTheComponentRetiredOrRetargeted: Retargeted, not retired. The obligation is real, current and legally operative: Iowa R. Crim. P. 2.80(3), 2.81(3) and 2.82(5) each require the application to be served on the county attorney, and Iowa R. Crim. P. 2.83(1) starts the county attorney's twenty-day response clock from service. A component that records what the participant must do belongs in the packet set. What is wrong is the document it names, not the role it plays.
determination.4_whatIsRetired: The standalone identity 'Certification of Service by Mailing or Delivery'. It names no published document, and the last reference to it is removed by retargeting the five components that carry it. Nothing else in the repository references it.
determination.5_dci76Target: ia-dci77-attachment-2 targets page 1 of the retained three-page Iowa Department of Public Safety combined packet at printed revision 9/22/21, pinned by sha256 321062c91b3d9e2c8f255d62d20186352a2b5884e0ccd4310a18a3a073d7f516. The component is not merged into DCI-77: they are genuinely different forms performing different functions on the same three pages, and the completed reconciliation is express that neither should be merged into the other.
determination.6_areEitherAcquisitionsStillRequired: No, and neither ever was. acquire:IA:certification-of-service-by-mailing-or-delivery cannot be satisfied by any issuer interaction because the Iowa Supreme Court has never prescribed a standalone document at that granularity. acquire:IA:dci-76-criminal-history-record-check-billing-form cannot be satisfied by a download because there is no separate DCI-76 binary to download; the bytes are retained and the edition disposition on the row already reads acquired_and_adopted. Both close without acquisition.
determination.7_isTheCertificationUnconditional: No. It is conditional on the paper-filing path and the form says so on its face: the boxed section opens "If you cannot find your case on the Iowa Judicial Branch eFile System, proceed with filing your application in paper at the county clerk of court office." Iowa Ct. R. 16.315(1)(b) provides that where a document is electronically filed EDMS serves it on all registered filers and no other service on those parties is required, so on the eFile path the applicant's own certification is unnecessary. Iowa Ct. R. 16.102(1) makes the conditionality coherent: a case pending before electronic filing began in that county is not subject to Chapter 16 at all, which is the case a participant cannot find on the system.
determination.8_isTheConditionalityFreeOfDoubt: No, and the doubt is recorded rather than smoothed. Read alone, Iowa Ct. R. 16.315(3)(a) — service on registered filers of documents filed by nonregistered filers is made by the clerk through EDMS — would make the applicant's certification redundant even on a paper filing, since county attorneys are registered filers. The form's own trigger language and rule 16.102(1) resolve it, but only when all three provisions are read together. How the packet expresses the condition to a participant is a legal-design question and is not decided here.
determination.9_areTheRule286FormsMandatory: No. Iowa R. Crim. P. 2.80(2), 2.81(2), 2.82(2), 2.82(3) and 2.82(4) each apply a substantial-compliance standard: an application "shall be initiated by completing and filing an application that substantially complies with" the named form. A substantially compliant application is legally sufficient.
determination.10_mayAMandatoryStatewideFlagBeCarriedFr: No, and this is the trap the reconciliation flagged. Iowa Ct. R. 17.1 makes the Chapter 17 self-represented-litigant forms mandatory in terms — persons without attorney representation "must use the forms listed in this chapter" — but the Rule 2.86 expungement forms are not in Chapter 17 and rule 17.1 does not reach them. Carrying a mandatory-statewide flag across would be wrong for all five bound tracks. No such flag is set here and none may be inferred from the retargeting: naming the parent form as the component's target records where the section lives, not that the form must be used verbatim.
determination.11_doesAnyIowaTrackBecomeReady: No. The five Rule 2.86 parent forms are themselves unmanifested and unretrieved, iowacourts.gov returns HTTP 403 to every automated request including its own privacy-policy page, the Iowa licensing position is unverified rather than silent, and no field map exists for any Iowa form. The Iowa official-PDF family stays fail-closed, generation is not permitted, runtime stays disabled and no packet becomes generatable.
determination.12_whatChangesInTheDenominator: Nothing. Six components stay six components across six tracks; Iowa keeps its seven normalized tracks. Two acquisition keys close, which reduces open acquisition rows by two and removes one phantom identity; five mapping blockers stop naming a document that does not exist and start naming one that does, which is a correction of their content and not a change in their number. The five mapping blockers themselves remain open, correctly, because the parent forms are unretrieved.

requiredAmendments.note: Each amendment is stated against the artifact that owns it and, where the artifact is generated, against the input field that produces it. None is applied by this job.

memo.whyTheMemoIsTheRealOwner: The track-source relationships are generated, not authored: sourceRelationships() emits one row per official_pdf_fill component and copies the component's officialFormId and officialSourceUrl straight through, taking sha256 from the track's officialSources entry whose url matches. Correcting the memo component is therefore the only way to correct the relationship row, and every generated consumer follows from it.

officialSourcesEntryToAdd.title: Iowa Department of Public Safety, Division of Criminal Investigation, combined Criminal History Record Check Billing Form (Form DCI-76, printed revision 9/22/21) and Criminal History Record Check Request Form (DCI-77), retained three-page fillable packet
officialSourcesEntryToAdd.whyThisEntryIsRequired: sourceRelationships() takes the row's sha256 from the track's officialSources entry whose url equals the component's officialSourceUrl. The ia-dci77 track currently has no officialSources entry for the packet path at all, which is why both of its generated rows read sha256 null even though the bytes are retained and measured. Adding this one entry pins the digest on ia-dci77-attachment-2 and, correctly, on ia-dci77-primary-filing-1 as well, because both forms are that one packet.
officialSourcesEntryToAdd.retrievedOnBasis: The date the queue row already records for the retained packet. This job retrieved nothing and asserts no new retrieval date.

dci76Component.notesToRecord: The billing form is page 1 of the retained three-page Department of Public Safety packet; DCI-77 is pages 2 to 3 of the same packet. Its own face states that a completed billing form is required when submitting any record-check request forms, that all forms are returned if it is incomplete, and that only one billing form is required when several request forms are submitted at one time. The record check this packet produces is a rule-mandated attachment: Iowa R. Crim. P. 2.81(2) requires a section 901C.3 application to be accompanied by an official Division of Criminal Investigation record check obtained on form DCI-77 with a release authorization signature and dated within the past thirty days.

whatTheMemoMustNotDo: Do not set any mandatory-use or mandatory-statewide flag on the Rule 2.86 forms. The standard is substantial compliance and Iowa Ct. R. 17.1 does not reach Chapter 2.
Do not merge DCI-76 into DCI-77 or delete either identity. They are different forms with different functions.
Do not delete the five certificate_of_service components. The service obligation is real and starts the county attorney's response clock.
Do not record a retrieval date, digest or byte count for any Rule 2.86 parent form. None has been retrieved and iowacourts.gov refuses automated requests.
Do not mark any Iowa track packet-ready, and do not change any track's outputStrategy or outputStrategyStatus. This is a source-binding correction, not a design change.

certificationRows.howItCloses: By removal of the last reference to the identity. certificationRows.currentnessQuestionAlreadyCorrect: The rows already read "No separately published certification-of-service form was located in the Iowa Judicial Branch forms collection; the certification appears within the Rule 2.86 application forms." That note was right as written; what was wrong was the requiredAcquisition instruction sitting beside it.

It does not exist. sourceIdentityConfidence document_identity_known is wrong for the same reason.
certificationRows.replacementMappingBlockers: Each of the five components keeps a mapping blocker under its existing dedupeKey — mapping:IA:<trackId>:<componentId> — now against its parent Rule 2.86 form, which is a real document that is genuinely unmanifested. The blockers do not disappear and must not.

fieldsThatContradictTheirOwnRationale.howItCorrects: Mechanically, once the component carries the retained packet URL. The reconciler reads the component's source binding; it recorded no_repository_binary because the component named no binary at all.

fieldsThatContradictTheirOwnRationale.recorded: Acquire the current official binary from the issuing authority and manifest it.
fieldsThatContradictTheirOwnRationale.correct: Nothing needs acquiring. The row's own edition12DispositionRationale already states that DCI-76 is published inside the same official packet Edition 1.2 retains under DCI-77, that there is no separate DCI-76 binary to acquire, and that what remains is a component-to-document mapping question.
fieldsThatContradictTheirOwnRationale.howItCorrects: The same way. A worker following the recorded instruction would attempt a retrieval the rationale on the same row explains is unnecessary, which is why this contradiction is worth closing rather than tolerating.

It may be a section of the Rule 2.86 forms rather than a standalone document, which is a component-identity question for a bounded legal-design pass.
rowsToClear.why: The bounded legal-design pass the row itself asked for has happened, and it answered the question in the affirmative. The row has no subject once the identity is gone.

The five Rule 2.86 parent forms and the Form 2 attached sheet are unretrieved and unmanifested. Nothing in this record touches them, and acquire:IA:rule-2-86-form-2-attached-sheet stays open.
It survives until the mapping is applied and a source-materialization receipt exists for the packet. Pinning a digest on a relationship is not materialization, and this job creates no receipt.
rowsThatMustSurvive.expectedDispositionAfterApplication: Resolvable, once the reconciler has run against the corrected memo and a receipt for the retained packet has been created by whoever owns materialization. Not resolvable by this record.

amendments.identity: Certification of Service by Mailing or Delivery
amendments.detail: The identity is recorded as identity_established_binary_unavailable with requiredAcquisition 'Acquire the current official binary from the issuing authority and manifest it.' Both assert a document exists and has merely not been obtained, which is affirmatively wrong. Retire the identity; do not re-manifest it, and never write a receipt for it. The role certificate_of_service is substantively correct and is not being corrected — it is the document binding that was wrong, not the role.

amendments.identity: DCI-76 Criminal History Record Check Billing Form
amendments.detail: Record that the identity is page 1 of the retained combined packet at printed revision 9/22/21 rather than an unacquired standalone document. No new bytes: the edition already records the disposition as acquired_and_adopted. The printed revision 9/22/21 applies to the whole artifact, so no revision correction is required.

participantFacingFindingsCarried.note: Three things the two resolutions surfaced that bear on what a participant is told or what an assembly emits. They are recorded here so they are not lost between lanes. None is decided here and none changes a packet today.

items.finding: The certification applies only where the case cannot be found on the Iowa Judicial Branch eFile System. On the eFile path, EDMS service under Iowa Ct. R. 16.315(1)(b) makes it unnecessary.
items.caveat: Iowa Ct. R. 16.315(3)(a) creates a tension the form text alone does not resolve. Any copy must be written from all three provisions together, not from the boxed text.

items.finding: The billing form's own face states that only one billing form is required when several request forms are submitted at one time. DCI-76 and DCI-77 are not a one-to-one pair.
items.owner: the Iowa legal-design and implementation lanes
items.consequenceIfIgnored: An assembly that emits one billing form per request form over-produces, and the participant sends the Division of Criminal Investigation something it does not ask for.
items.notDecidedHere: How the packet expresses the cardinality is a legal-design and assembly question. This record states the rule and stops.

items.finding: Iowa R. Crim. P. 2.81(2) requires the Division of Criminal Investigation record check accompanying a section 901C.3 application to be dated within the past thirty days.
items.consequence: It is a real sequencing constraint: the record check must be obtained close enough to filing that it is still current when the application is filed. Recorded as an observation; not decided here.

premiseCorrectionsCarried.recorded: ia-7251 concerns Iowa Code § 907.9 deferred judgment.
premiseCorrectionsCarried.verified: ia-7251 maps to Rule 2.86—Form 5, Application to Expunge Prostitution Court Records under Iowa Code section 725.1.
